questions.q: In an immunocompetent child with PSGN, the usual age range is:
Fill up: The common PSGN organism is group A beta-haemolytic ______.
Match infection with typical interval — 1) sore throat 2) skin infection 3) IRGN in a diabetic … A) alongside infection B) 7–10 days C) 2–4 weeks
The most frequent presentation of PSGN is acute proliferative glomerulonephritis with low C3.
On immunofluorescence during the clinical phase of PSGN, the characteristic pattern is:
opts: Granular IgG + C3 in capillary walls more than mesangium
questions.exp: Granular IgG + C3 in capillary walls more than mesangium. (Book p776)

questions.q: The subepithelial deposits in PSGN electron microscopy are called:
Fill up: In PSGN, amlodipine for hypertension is given at ______ mg.
A child with active PSGN has pulmonary oedema. The book's treatment table pairs this sign with:
questions.exp: Diuretics, such as torsemide 5–10 mg. (Book p776)

questions.q: For an active sore throat in PSGN, a listed single-dose antibiotic regimen is:
questions.exp: 1.2 million units of benzathine penicillin. (Book p777)

questions.q: Fill up: With prompt treatment, ______% of PSGN patients recover in 3–5 days.
A persistent microscopic haematuria after treatment of PSGN is described as:
opts: It may persist and has no significance
questions.exp: It may persist and has no significance. (Book p777)

questions.q: Match the following — 1) first item 2) second item 3) third item … A) Abrupt onset with high BP and RBC casts B) Insidious onset with normal BP C) Marked proteinuria with low albumin
opts: Abrupt onset with high BP and RBC casts
questions.exp: Abrupt onset with high BP and RBC casts. (Book p777)
